scope: Shared one-entry dispatch ownership for CSR/MRET/WFI and a temporary serialized load/store integration path. The production CSR caller uses this block; memory metadata is tested with synthetic rename/ROB acceptance only. Production memory classification, IQ/LSQ scheduling, address preparation, bus requests and memory retirement are not connected by this task. Stalling all younger dispatch behind memory is a temporary staging policy, not the final architecture memory scheduling contract. No full-core memory acceptance, formal proof or clock claim.
dispatch: valid_i is a lane-zero prefix. serial_i classifies head-owned operations after frontend-fault override; cfi0_i classifies lane-zero CFI. Ordinary pairs pass through. Lane-zero serialized operation is admitted alone; lane-one serialized operation is deferred while lane zero proceeds. CFI lane zero cuts the tail. dispatch_valid_o is an offered prefix; other resources reserve it atomically. Feed dispatch_solo_o to ROB allocation and exclude serial_i lanes from IQ insertion/credits. Held ownership blocks all younger allocation while older IQ work may continue. memory_i classifies only the accepted lane-zero owner; it is ignored otherwise.
capture: Capture only actual accepted lane-zero serialized allocation: full 13-bit ROB identity, original instruction/PC, class bit and both renamed source tags. owner_sources_o packs {source2,source1}, six bits each, directly matching issue_backend.head_source_i. The class bit owner_memory_o distinguishes memory from CSR/MRET/WFI and remains stable while held. Later offered tags or class cannot replace owned metadata. ROB retains destination ownership; this holder does not capture values or a destination tag.
head: owner_valid_o requires a held descriptor, live head, exact generation+slot identity and matching PC, with no reset/flush/drain/recovery. This qualifies later PRF/head-controller ownership, not operand readiness. Consumers qualify the saved class before steering execution. busy_o and saved owner metadata remain visible until release/cancellation; invalid owner metadata is zero. Read data/readiness must not feed combinationally back into read ownership.
release: Only actual successful retirement with matching full identity releases normally, using retire_accept_i and retire_id_i. Descriptor preparation, memory request acceptance and result arrival are not release events. Faulting operations remain owned until accepted trap recovery drives flush_i. No same-cycle refill or younger dispatch is allowed. Reset/full flush cancels ownership. CSR and memory side effects are outside this block.
recovery: recover_i denotes an already validated and accepted branch recovery; recover_slot_i is the branch slot and head_id_i supplies the pre-cycle head. Modulo-32 order kills only a younger descriptor, suppressing every new offer that cycle. Older/equal descriptors are retained. killed_o reports cancellation for the future head-controller connection. Full reset/flush dominates retirement. Slot-only recovery is valid only with upstream generation/live-branch validation. Recovery cannot coincide with accepted retirement.
drain: drained_i suppresses new transactions and requires no held descriptor. Coordinator must also check external IQ/producer/ROB/frontend holders; this block does not implement global identity drain.
source_rules: The caller uses the shared decoder and rename outputs. memory_i=0 permits CSR/MRET/WFI and ordinary FENCE only, with source2=p0; immediate CSR, MRET, WFI, FENCE and rs1=x0 also use source1=p0. FENCE.I remains unsupported. memory_i=1 permits LB/LH/LW/LBU/LHU/SB/SH/SW only. Every load uses source2=p0 regardless of instruction immediate bits; every memory rs1=x0 uses source1=p0; stores with rs2=x0 use source2=p0. Unused/x0 implies p0 is a caller assertion, not a new synthesized decoder or full rename proof. Loads to rd=x0 remain captured operations.
